newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Maori TV probe calls for conditions on funding.
newsitem.headline: NZ Maori TV probe calls for conditions on funding.

text.p: A Commerce Ministry report into Maori television station Aotearoa Television (ATN) released on Wednesday said future funding should be conditional on the station meeting agreed standards of financial management.

"Significant improvement needs to be made to ATN's financial management and any future funding should be conditional on agreed standards being met," the report by Commerce Secretary Paul Carpinter said.
On Monday Cabinet reversed its decision to provide NZ$4 million in funding to the station after a verbal report of the ministry's findings was given to Communications Minister Maurice Williamson.

The report, dated February 10, followed a series of allegations that the station's asset were bought at inflated values and that some directors spent thousands of dollars on clothing at the company's expense.

The report concluded Maori Broadcasting agency Te Mangai Paho (TMP) had acted lawfully in funding production services by ATN, but said TMP's ownership of the transmitter used by the station "would not appear to come within the scope of the statutory functions" of TMP.
It also noted a significant conflict of interest because a TMP Auckland staff member's partner worked in a non-management role at ATN.

"The TMP staff member in Auckland provides an important monitoring role for TMP. While other conflicts of interest appear to have been adequately dealt with by TMP, a conflict in this monitoring role is of more concern and should be considered further by TMP," the report said.
The report said Aotearoa Television has exceeded the performance criteria required by TMP.

It said TMP should have told Communications Minister Maurice Williamson of its concerns about the overall financial management of Aotearoa in mid-January before any future funding decisions were made.
Carpinter said Aotearoa's current financial position was uncertain.
"Establishing the true position is now made very difficult by the requisitioning of ATN's financial records by the Serious Fraud Office," he said.
The spokeswoman for the Serious Fraud Office said an investigation into Aotearoa was underway but no date had been set for the release of its findings.
